code.originalText: Day 1 of cycle 2 of dostarlimab: early response, immune-related adverse event checks, germline and tumor genetic results, iron and anemia, and golf

text.paragraph: Ms. Didrikson Zaharias comes before her second dose of dostarlimab. The first dose three weeks ago caused no reaction. Within ten days the bleeding became occasional streaks, and for the last week there has been none; her stools are a normal shape and the urgency has eased. She has had no diarrhea, rash, cough, breathlessness, headache or thirst. She has taken ferrous sulfate every other morning for four weeks, with mild constipation that settled with more fruit, and she is less tired. She is practicing every day and played 18 holes twice last week. The germline panel was negative, and tumor sequencing found two changes in MSH2 in the tumor itself, which explains the mismatch repair deficiency. She asked what this means for her brothers and sisters. [S]

list.item:
Low rectal adenocarcinoma, mismatch repair deficient, on dostarlimab (C20). An early clinical response after one dose: the bleeding has stopped, the tumor is smaller to the finger, and CEA has fallen from 5.8 to 3.4 ng/mL. No immune-related adverse event; thyroid, liver and kidney tests normal. The germline panel found no pathogenic variant in MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, EPCAM or the other colorectal cancer genes, and tumor sequencing found two somatic MSH2 variants, so this is a sporadic mismatch repair-deficient cancer rather than Lynch syndrome. Her first-degree relatives still have a raised risk because she had colorectal cancer young, and are advised to start colonoscopy at 40, or 10 years before her age at diagnosis if that is earlier, and repeat it every five years. Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests were negative; hepatitis B surface antibody was negative, so vaccination is due. [S]
Dostarlimab cycle 2 today.
A letter for her to share with her brothers and sisters, if she chooses, explaining their screening.
Restaging MRI, sigmoidoscopy and examination after four doses.

Iron deficiency anemia from rectal blood loss (D50.0). Hemoglobin up from 11.1 to 12.1 g/dL and MCV from 77 to 80 fL four weeks after starting oral iron, with the bleeding stopped. [S]
Continue ferrous sulfate every other morning.
Ferritin at about three months.
